IF YOU WILL NOT HOLD THE FULL DIPLOMA

Not every IB student leaves with the Diploma. Take individual Diploma Programme subjects, or sit the Diploma and miss its conditions, and the IB awards DP Course Results instead — a real qualification, read differently from a Diploma rather than not read at all.

Asks for the full Diploma — 50 of 73. Reachable on Course Results — 23 of 73.

Asking for the Diploma is not the same as closing the door, and where a source publishes another way in it is written here.

It does not close this one to you. The Danish Agency treats DP Course Results of at least 18 points, with at least grade 3 in all six subjects and at least three of them at HL, as equivalent to a qualifying examination for a Danish university bachelor once you have added two successive raises in the level of upper-secondary subjects, at least one of them to A level, taken as hf-enkeltfag or as a self-study candidate. If you already hold an A-level subject other than Danish, two raises to B level are enough. Retaking to be awarded the full IB Diploma is the other published route.

It does not close this one to you, and Breda is the only institution in this catalogue whose own rules open a door before you turn 21. BUas admits on a havo- or vwo-equivalent diploma, and its list of international qualifications gives the IB exactly two entries — the Career-related Certificate against havo, the IB Diploma against vwo — with nothing for Course Results. What it publishes instead is the 21+ assessment, run under article 7.29 of the Dutch Higher Education Act: a computer-based capability test of your mathematical, linguistic and spatial skills, 150 euro, sat on 4 February and 15 April 2027, passed at 5 of 9 points, valid for two years and only at BUas. You apply for the programme through Studielink first — by 1 May at the latest — then answer the extra questions in My Online Application or email studentoffice@buas.nl saying you do not meet the entry requirements; an English test is still required on top of it, and a failed assessment cannot be resat the same year. Normally you must be 21 when the programme starts. The exception is the part worth writing to them about: BUas's own Regeling aanmelding en inschrijving says the Executive Board "kan besluiten de studiekiezer, die in het bezit is van een buiten Nederland afgegeven getuigschrift, deel te laten nemen aan het toelatingsonderzoek, ook indien de leeftijd van 21 jaar nog niet bereikt is" — it may let the holder of a qualification issued outside the Netherlands sit the entrance assessment before 21, and the same applies in special cases where no diploma can be produced. DP Course Results are a document issued outside the Netherlands and Nuffic calls them a transcript rather than a diploma. Nothing says BUas will use that discretion for you — the verb is "kan besluiten" and the decision is the Board's — so put the question to studentoffice@buas.nl in writing and early, name the article, and keep a plan that does not depend on the answer. One further route is national rather than this institution's, and it is the only one that produces the qualification itself instead of an exemption from it: the Dutch staatsexamen vwo. It does not close this one to you.
